context.publicQuote: As commercial rents go up, venues are driven out of business, destroying opportunities for musicians.

Street vendors are the smallest businesses in NYC. And they’re an essential component of our neighborhoods. The Commercial Rent Stabilization bill is the first step needed in protecting our small businesses.
My two stores did not close because of Amazon - my business was thriving. It was because of unreasonable rent.

We see thriving community spaces shuttered overnight due to doubling and tripling rents. Commercial tenants invest in our neighborhoods, provide work and services, and reflect our culture. Commercial rent stabilization is an important step toward achieving an equitable, diverse, and just city.

Time and time again we’ve seen businesses shutter in my district and throughout the city due to rent increases. This bill helps establish basic rights for commercial tenants so the businesses that are a vital part of our communities can continue to serve our communities and thrive.
When you give small businesses a fighting chance, you give whole neighborhoods a fighting chance
We’re here to support Commercial Rent Stabilization because landlords like ours should not be able to abuse the power against small businesses like ours.

Losing the independently-owned small businesses that we love, one after another, tears at the fabric of our communities. If we want to preserve what is best about our communities, amidst skyrocketing rents we must take bold action now.
This place was so good.

I own a off broadway stage production business. My rent has doubled since 2008. I've been thinking about leaving the city because it's getting so expensive. If my rent is expensive then they have to pass the costs to the off broadway productions.
it's everywhere, all the small places are closing. I only have so much money.
I worked 9/11 Recovery. I got cancer because of it and now I'm struggling to pay my medical bills. I live frugally, but it's hard when neighborhood stores are so expensive now.
This was a business owned by two African women for 20 years. Their rent went up and now they're gone.
We've lived here for 40 years, and everything's closing. You lose community. This use to all be open, now the little spaces are all closed. Its all Starbucks, Starbucks, Starbucks.
Our rent is going up, and thats why we've got to go.
My friend had a place that was $2,000, they raised it to $5,000, and he had to close. You either pay the rent or you close, what are you going to do?
This bike shop closed?? My friend used to come here.

I worked at bookbook when they moved to this space in 2009 because their old landlord wanted to raise the rent 800%. Just 10 years later they had to close. Commercial Rent Stabilization would have kept this bookstore open longer, meanwhile this space has been vacant for 6 months.
All these places on the block closed because the rent went up.
My hardware store has been open 43 years. Now they've raised my rent 3 times in 2 years. How are you going to stay in business?
You could even be blind and notice the issue of all these places closing.
Speculative landlords are just thinking about numbers on a page, not relationships or community. What should I do next?
The dry cleaner next door was here for 20 years and closed too because the rent went up.
All the storefronts along this street are vacant
My rent has more than doubled since I opened up.
My father started this place 18 years ago. The rent has more than trippled. This is the Bronx, its middle class. You can't overcharge people.
We used to have two stores, but had to close down one last year because the rent went up. Now we’re worried because the lease ends next month on this store. So this law would really help.
I remember when Vic's was here. Commercial Rent Stabilization is important because otherwise we’ll only have TD bank and Walgreens.
I have been saying for years we need Commercial Rent Stabilization.
I want to do my part.
I am a landlord and I support commercial rent stabilization. We also need to stabilize the costs for landlords.
We are greenpoint kids. So many great old polish businesses have closed. We have to do something about it. We don’t want just Starbucks.
This storefront has been vacant for two years.

I know they take advantage of commercials. We used to have a store in brooklyn too. We were there for 40 years, but they tripled the rent and were asking for $100,000 to sign a lease. We had to close.
We need this. We have a new landlord and we don’t know what will happen. We used to have the place next door too, but the rent went up and we have to move.
